sources.entry: uarch-bench - Isolates memory-level parallelism from load latency as separate tests, with DVFS held off before timing, x86 Linux only.

summary.one_liner: uarch-bench is a C++/NASM collection of fine-grained x86 Linux microbenchmarks for probing CPU micro-architectural behavior and timing small functions repeatably.
summary.what_it_does: The project provides a set of low-level benchmarks (assembly and some C++) that target specific micro-architectural features such as dependency chains, store and load behavior, pointer chasing, prefetch instructions, BMI false dependencies, and VZEROALL effects. It includes a framework for timing code, converting measurements to cycles, removing outliers, and running tests over parameter ranges such as buffer sizes. Benchmarks are grouped (for example basic, memory/load-parallel, memory/store-parallel, memory/pointer-chase, bmi, studies/vzeroall) and results are reported in cycles and nanoseconds. A wrapper script, uarch-bench.sh, tries to disable turbo boost or frequency scaling while running and restores the previous setting afterward. The README says that with libpfc enabled (USE_LIBPFC=1) Intel performance counters can be read across the timed region. Benchmarks that need unavailable CPU features, such as AVX-512, are skipped at runtime.
use_cases: measure cycle costs of individual x86 instructions
study cache size transitions with load and store sweeps
investigate store-to-load and store buffer effects
time small assembly or C++ idioms repeatably
how_to_run: git clone --recursive https://github.com/travisdowns/uarch-bench (or run: git submodule update --init in an existing clone)
notable: Sweeps buffer sizes (16 KiB to 32 MiB) to show cache-level transitions in load, store, and prefetch throughput
Wrapper script disables turbo boost or frequency scaling during runs and restores the prior setting afterward
Optional libpfc mode reads Intel performance counters across the timed region, reportedly to single-cycle precision
Reports results in cycles and nanoseconds and skips tests whose required CPU features are missing
Includes a framework for adding new micro-benchmarks
caveats: Supports only x86 Linux; Windows and macOS are not yet supported according to the README
Work-in-progress with limited documentation and testing, per the README disclaimer
Best results need root for frequency scaling control and libpfc mode; non-root runs have limitations and leave frequency scaling alone
